Praises sing! Sing your praises unto God! Sing His praise! 
Lift your voices and sing praises to our King!

The LORD ascended while the trumpets rang with happy tone,
For God is King of all the earth; Sing praise to Him alone.
God rules the nations; God is seated on His holy throne.
 Praises sing! Sing your praises unto God! Sing His praise! 
Lift your voices and sing praises to our King!

The LORD is great, great praise deserving
Within the city of our God;
His holy hill, raised up in beauty,
Brings joy to all the earth abroad.

Mount Zion is the great King’s city
And heaven’s one true mountain height;
Within her palaces is safety,
For God protects her by His might.

And at that place, like one in labor,
They shook, for they with fear were seized.
You are the One who ships from Tarshish
Destroys by wind sent from the east.

What we had heard of our God’s city,
We now have seen and know for sure,
The city of the LORD of Armies,
Which God forever makes secure.

hymns.title: The LORD Is Great
hymns.composer: Gottfried W. Fink, 1842; arr. Arthur S. Sullivan

verses.text:
The LORD is great, and so His praise
Should be proclaimed abroad
Within His hill of holiness,
The city of our God.
Mount Zion’s beauty is raised high,
Earth joys on her account.
It is the city of our King, 
The one true heav’nly mount.

Well known among her palaces,
God is her refuge strong.
Behold, when kings joined forces there, 
Together they passed on.
For what they saw left them amazed 
And filled with deep dismay;
So troubled were they at the sight
They turned and ran away.

With fear and anguish they were seized,
As one whom birth pains take;
And You with wind out of the east,
The ships of Tarshish break.
As we have heard, we’ve seen within 
God’s city most secure;
The city of the LORD of hosts,
Our God keeps evermore.

Within Your temple we have thought
Upon Your love, O God.
As is Your name, O God, Your praise
Is spread through earth abroad.
As is Your name, O God, Your praise
Is spread through earth abroad.

Your right hand holds all righteousness.
Mount Zion’s joy be great!
Let Judah’s daughters joyfully
Your judgments celebrate.
Let Judah’s daughters joyfully
Your judgments celebrate.

Encircle Zion, walk about,
And mark her towers well;
Consider her protective walls,
Behold her citadels.
 Consider her protective walls,
Behold her citadels.

Thus you may generations tell,
For what a God is He!
He is our God for evermore,
Who guides eternally.
He is our God for evermore,
Who guides eternally.

Why should I fear evil days 
When my foes’ sin surrounds;
Even those who trust their wealth, 
Who boast as it abounds?
No man can by any means, 
Pay to God his ransom price;
For the purchase of his soul
No payment can suffice.

There is nothing one can do
To live eternally
So that he will never die
Nor will corruption see.
For he sees that wise men die,
Fools and senseless perish too;
They will leave their wealth behind
For other men to use.

Yet they think within themselves 
Their homes will always be;
By their names they call their lands, 
So ev’ry age will see.
But man’s honor will not last; 
Like the beasts, he too will end.
Thus will be the way of fools
And those who them commend.

Just like sheep, their destiny
Will be within the grave;
Death’s their shepherd, just men rule 
O’er them with each new day.
And the grave consumes their strength; 
It no habitation leaves.
Yet will God redeem my soul, 
From death’s grip me receives.

hymns.title: Let No Fear Disturb Your Peace
hymns.firstLine: Let No Fear Disturb Your Peace
hymns.composer: Attributed to Martin Herbst, Numbergisches Gesangbuch, 1676

verses.text:
Though throughout the time he lives,
To himself he praises gives - 
And though men will praise you too,
When good things for self you do -

To his fathers he will go,
Where the eye no light will know.
Man with honor, yet not wise,
Like the beasts that perish, dies.

God, Most Supreme in Might,
The One who is the LORD,
Assembles earth from east to west
By His own spoken word.

From Zion, beautiful,
God shines forth gloriously.
Our God most surely coming is
And will not silent be.

Fire burns at His approach,
And storms around Him rage;
He summons heav’n and earth, that He
May His own people judge.

“My consecrated ones
Before Me gathered be,
Those who by sacrifice have made
A covenant with Me.”

Heaven above proclaims
His righteousness abroad,
Because He is Himself the judge;
There is no judge but God.

O you, My people, hear!
I’ll speak and testify
Against you now, O Israel;
For God, your God, am I.

I’m not rebuking you
For lack of sacrifice;
Nor for burnt off’rings which you place
Each day before My eyes.

I need no bull nor goat
Which you in pens confine;
For cattle on a thousand hills,
And all wild beasts, are Mine.

Birds in the mountains high
Are all to Me well known;
The beasts that roam the wilds untamed,
They, too, are all My own.

If I were hungry now
I would not speak to you,
Because the world belongs to Me,
And all that’s in it, too.

Will I eat flesh of bulls?
Or goats’ blood drink will I?
Make thankfulness your sacrifice;
Pay vows to God Most High.

And always call on Me
The day you trouble see;
For I will then deliver you
That you may honor Me.

But to the wicked one
God says, “What right have you
To take My cov’nant in your mouth
My statutes to declare?
For discipline you hate,
You cast My words away.
You see and give support to thieves;
You join adulterers.

Your mouth with evil filled,
Your tongue produces lies.
Against your brother you speak out
To shame your mother’s son.
And when I did not speak, 
You thought I was like you;
But I’ll accuse you now and state
My case before your eyes.

Consider this with care,
All you who God forget,
Or I will tear you limb from limb,
And none will rescue you.
One honors Me who brings
A sacrifice of praise;
To one who rightly sets his way
I’ll God’s salvation show.”

God, be merciful to me; 
On Your love I rest my plea.
By Your vast abounding grace,
My transgressions all erase.
From the stain of every sin,
Wash, and make me clean within.

For my sins before me rise,
Always present to my eyes.
I have sinned ’gainst You alone,
In Your sight I’ve evil done;
So Your words are proven true,
Righteous are Your judgments, too.

Truly, I was born in sin,
Sinful when conceived within.
Surely You desire to find
Faithfulness in heart and mind;
You will, deep within my heart, 
Wisdom unto me impart.

O with hyssop sprinkle me,
And from sin I clean will be;
Wash me from its stain, and so,
I’ll be whiter than the snow.
Make me hear joy’s cheering voice,
Let the bones You crushed rejoice.

O hide Your face from all my sin,
And wipe my guilt from view.
A clean heart make for me, O God;
My spirit’s strength renew.
O from Your presence cast me not,
Your face no more to see;
Your Holy Spirit then, I pray,
Take not away from me.

The joy which Your salvation brings
Again to me restore;
And with a willing spirit then
Uphold me evermore.
Then I transgressors will instruct
That they Your ways may learn,
And those who now abide in sin
To You they will return.

O free me from bloodguiltiness,
O God, my Savior, God!
Then I Your perfect righteousness
With joyful tongue will laud.
My lips which have so long been closed
May You now open, Lord;
And when You have restored my speech,
I will You praise accord.

No sacrifice do you desire,
Or it I’d surely bring;
And certainly You are not pleased
With whole burnt offering.
A broken spirit is to God
A pleasing sacrifice;
A broken and a contrite heart,
O God, You’ll not despise.

With loving favor by You shown
Make Zion’s goodness sure.
The walls of Your Jerusalem
Build up to heights secure.
Then You’ll delight in sacrifice,
Burnt off’rings day by day,
With whole burnt off’rings and young bulls,
Which on Your altar lay.

God, be merciful to me; 
On Your love I rest my plea.
By Your vast abounding grace,
My transgressions all erase.
From the stain of every sin,
Wash, and make me clean within.

For my sins before me rise,
Always present to my eyes.
I have sinned ’gainst You alone,
In Your sight I’ve evil done;
So Your words are proven true,
Righteous are Your judgments, too.

Truly, I was born in sin,
Sinful when conceived within.
Surely You desire to find
Faithfulness in heart and mind;
You will, deep within my heart, 
Wisdom unto me impart.

O, with hyssop sprinkle me,
And from sin I clean will be.
Wash me from its stain, and so,
I’ll be whiter than the snow.
Make me hear joy’s cheering voice,
Let the bones You crushed rejoice.

hymns.title: From My Sins, O Hide Your Face
hymns.firstLine: From My Sins, O Hide Your Face

verses.text:
Give salvation’s joy again,
And a willing mind sustain.
Then Your perfect ways I’ll show
That transgressors may them know;
Sinners are converted then, 
Turning back to You again.

From bloodguiltiness, O God
Set me free, my Savior, God.
Then my tongue will joy express,
Singing of Your righteousness.
Open now my lips, O Lord;
From my mouth will praise be poured.

Sacrifice You will not take,
Or the off’ring I would make.
Off’rings burnt bring no delight,
But a broken heart, contrite,
God’s accepted sacrifice,
You, O God, will not despise.

Why boast of wrong, O mighty man?
God’s love endures all day.
Your tongue plots evil; razor sharp,
From truth it goes astray.
You cherish evil more than good,
And falsehood more than right.
You cherish all devouring words;
Your tongue in lies delights.

Forever God will break you down,
Will seize you with His hand,
Will tear you from your dwelling place,
Uproot you from the land.
The just will see and laugh and say, 
 “He’d not make God his strength, 
But his abundant wealth he’d trust;
His malice gave him strength.”

But I within the house of God
Am like an olive tree;
And in the steadfast love of God
My trust will always be.
Forever I will give You thanks,
What You have done proclaim;
In presence of Your godly ones
I’ll wait on Your good name.

hymns.title: Mighty Man, Why Boast in Evil?
hymns.firstLine: Mighty Man, Why Boast in Evil?

verses.text:
Mighty man, why boast in evil?
For God’s mercy is all day long.
With your tongue you plot destruction,
Like a razor, you work deceit.
You love evil more than goodness,
And deceit more than truthful words.
You love all words with destructive pow’r 
O you sharp and deceitful tongue.

God will break you down forever,
Seize and tear you from where you live.
By your roots He then will pull you
From the land of all living men.
Just men see with awe, yet laughing,
“This man would not make God his trust,
But he trusted his abundant wealth,
And in malice he gained his strength.”

But in God’s house I am growing
Like a green fruitful olive tree.
Without ceasing I am trusting
In the firm loyal love of God.
I will give You thanks forever,
For it’s You that has done all this;
In Your good name I will set my hope
In the midst of Your godly ones.

hymns.title: The Fool Says in His Heart
hymns.firstLine: The Fool Says in His Heart

verses.text:
The fool says in his heart,
“There is not any God.”
They are corrupt. Their deeds are vile;
There’s no one who does good.

From heaven God looks down
On sons of men abroad
To see if any understands,
If any seeks for God.

Those working wickedness -
Do they not know at all,
Who eat My people as their bread,
And on God do not call?

Let Isr’el’s rescue come, 
From Zion help now bring; 
When God restores His captive ones,
Let Jacob, Isr’el, sing.

hymns.title: The Fool Has Spoken in His Heart
hymns.firstLine: The Fool Has Spoken in His Heart

verses.text:
The fool has spoken in his heart,
“There surely is no God.”
Unjust, abhorrent works they do,
Intending to cause harm.
Not one of them does good.

God gazes down from heaven high
Upon the human race,
To see what their behavior is.
Does any understand?
Does any seek God’s face?

Each from the right way turned aside
To have his own way done.
Together they became corrupt,
Not one of them does good,
No, not a single one.

But these who work such wickedness,
Do they not know at all?
Do they just eat my people up
The way they eat their bread?
On God they do not call.

Where once they had no cause to fear,
There they are terrorized.
God strewed the bones of these your foes.
And you have caused them shame,
Since God has them despised.

From Zion who will come to save,
And help to Isr’el bring?
God brings His captive people back!
Then Jacob will rejoice,
And Isr’el shout and sing!

See how God has been my helper,
How my Lord sustains my soul:
To my foes He pays back evil - 
In Your truth destroy them all!
I will sacrifice with gladness;
Your good name I’ll praise, O LORD. 
He has saved me from all trouble;
I have looked on all my foes.

hymns.title: By Your Name, O God
hymns.composer: Traditional Welsh melody; arr. Thomas J. Williams, 1890

verses.text:
See how God has been my helper,
How my Lord sustains my soul:
To my foes He pays back evil - 
In Your truth destroy them all!
I will sacrifice with gladness;
Your good name I’ll praise, O LORD. 
He has saved me from all trouble;
I have looked on all my foes.

Give ear to this my prayer, O God,
And hide not from my cry.
Give answer, for I cannot rest,
But must complain and sigh;

Because I hear the voice of foes,
And wicked ones oppress
To bring their evil down on me - 
Such hatred they express!

Now anguish is within my heart
Of death and agony.
I’m touched with trembling and with fear,
And horror seizes me.

I said, “O make me like a dove,
With wings to fly away,
That I might find another place
To dwell in and to stay.”

“For then I’d wander far and rest
In some lone desert waste;
From stormy wind and tempest fierce,
I would escape in haste.”

hymns.title: Consume the Wicked
hymns.composer: Georg F. Handel, 1748; harm. Austin C. Lovelace, b. 1919

verses.text:
Consume the wicked, O my Lord;
Confuse their tongues, divide;
For in the city I’ve seen strife
And violence abide.
For day and night upon her walls
The city they surround,
While mischief and iniquity
Inside of her are found.

A realm of vast destruction thrives
Within her very heart;
And from her streets oppression, fraud, 
And graft do not depart.
It was no foe reproaching me,
For that I could endure;
It was no hater rising up,
Or I could hide secure.

But it is you, a man, a friend,
My colleague all along!
We shared sweet fellowship and walked
To God’s house in the throng.
Let death now come upon them all,
To Sheol they’ll depart;
For wickedness is in their house,
And lives within their heart.

hymns.title: But as for Me, I’ll Call on God
hymns.firstLine: But as for Me, I’ll Call on God

verses.text:
But as for me, I’ll call on God, 
Because the LORD saves me;
At evening, morning, and at noon,
He hears my cry and plea.
And He redeems my soul unharmed
That I at peace may be
Through all the war against me waged,
For many strive with me.

But God will hear and punish them - 
He ever sits enthroned - 
Because they never change their ways;
No fear of God have shown.
My friend profaned his covenant,
His heart was full of war.
Though smooth as oil the words he spoke,
Yet sharp and like a sword.

Cast all your burden on the LORD
And He will you sustain;
For He makes sure that still unmoved
The righteous will remain.
O God, into destruction’s pit,
By You they have been thrust;
Deceitful killers won’t live long,
But You will be my trust.

hymns.title: Be Merciful to Me, O God
hymns.firstLine: Be Merciful to Me, O God
hymns.composer: John Wyeth, Repository of Sacred Music, II, 1813

verses.text:
Be merciful to me, O God,
For man has hounded me;
He fights against me all day long, 
To crush me utterly.
My foes pursue me all day long,
In pride wage war on me.

When fearful, I will trust in God
Whose word I do revere.
In God I’ve always put my trust,
No terror will come near.
What can a mortal do to me
That I could ever fear?

hymns.title: You Have Recorded All My Ways
hymns.firstLine: You Have Recorded All My Ways

verses.text:
In God whose word I give my praise,
The LORD’s word I revere,
In God I now have put my trust,
So I will have no fear.
In God is where my trust will be;
What can man do to me?

Your vows are binding on me, God,
I’ll render thanks to You.
For You have saved my soul from death,
My feet from stumbling, too.
So I will walk before God’s sight 
With life and in its light.

hymns.title: Be Merciful to Me, O God
hymns.firstLine: Be Merciful to Me, O God

verses.text:
Be merciful to me, O God,
Be merciful to me,
Because my soul has found in You
Its true security.

I’m safe in shadow of Your wings
’Til ruin passes by;
I’ll cry to God who gives me help, 
I’ll call to God Most High.

From heaven He will send and save,
Shaming those hounding me.
His lovingkindness God will send,
And ever faithful be.

My soul among the lions lies,
With men who lust for war;
With those whose teeth are spears and darts,
Whose tongues are sharpened swords.

hymns.title: O Be Exalted High, O God
hymns.firstLine: O Be Exalted High, O God

verses.text:
They spread a net to catch my feet;
My soul was bowed with dread.
Although they dug a pit for me,
They fell in it instead.

My heart is firm, my heart is firm,
O God, I’ll praise with song.
My glory wake! Wake harp and lyre!
My song will wake the dawn.

And I will offer thanks to You
Among the peoples, Lord;
And I among the nations will
With song my praise sound forth.

Because Your cov’nant love is great,
It reaches heaven high;
And Your unfailing faithfulness
Extends up to the sky.

O be exalted high, O God!
Above the heavens stand,
And let Your glory be above
All earth, both sea and land.

hymns.title: Gods, Do You Really Speak with Righteousness?
hymns.firstLine: Gods, Do You Really Speak with Righteousness?

verses.text:
Gods, do you really speak with righteousness?
Do you uprightly judge, O sons of men?   
No! In your heart you work unrighteousness;
On earth you weigh out violence from your hands.

The wicked are estranged ev’n from the womb; 
These who speak lies have wandered since their birth.
They have the venom of a deafened snake,
Which does not even hear its charmer’s spells.

Let them be as a moving snail that melts;
Like stillborn babes, let them not see the sun. 
Before your pots feel heat from burning thorns, 
The wicked, green or dry, He blows away.

hymns.title: Do You, Gods, Speak Righteousness?
hymns.composer: John Bishop, 1711; harm. Harry E. Woolridge, 1845-1917

verses.text:
Do you, O gods, speak righteousness?
Do you the people justly judge?
No! You delight in doing wrong;
You violence deal out with your hand.
The wicked, from the womb estranged,
Are liars, straying since their birth.

They have the venom of a snake,
And like a serpent close their ears.
They cannot hear the charmer’s song,
Though skillfully he casts a spell.
O God, now shatter all their teeth;
Destroy young lions’ teeth, O LORD.

Like waters let them drain away;
And let their arrows blunted be.
Let them be like a melting slug,
Or stillborns never seeing day.
Before your pots can feel the fire,
He blows the burning thorns away.

With joy the just one vengeance sees,
And treads in blood of wicked men.
Thus people will be brought to say, 
“The just will surely have reward.
It’s surely true there is a God
Who justly judges on the earth.”

Arouse to meet me and behold my plight.
LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, 
Awake to punish nations everywhere;
To wicked, treach’rous men, no favor show.

They come at evening snarling like a dog;
And they encircle all the city wall.
See evil things that spew forth from their mouth - 
Their lips are swords; they think You will not hear.

hymns.title: I Wait for You
hymns.composer: Jean Sibelius, 1899; arr. David Hugh Jones, 1955

verses.text:
I wait for You, because You are my strength,
A mighty fort, a stronghold is my God.
My loving God, my God, will meet with me,
And let me look in triumph on my foes.
Spare them, O Lord, our Shield, lest we forget;
But in Your might disperse and bring them down.

hymns.title: O God, You Have Rejected Us
hymns.firstLine: O God, You Have Rejected Us

verses.text:
O God, You have rejected us,
And broken us once more.
As You’ve been angry with us all;
O once again restore!

As You have caused the earth to quake,
And torn it open wide;
O heal its gaping cracks because
It rocks from side to side.

And You have made the people know 
The hardness of distress;
And You have made them drink the wine
Of reeling drunkenness.

A banner You have given those
Who look to You with fear;
Let it before us be unfurled,
And so let truth appear.

O grant that those You’ve dearly loved
May all delivered be;
O save them with Your strong right hand,
And answer give to me.

God in His holiness declared, 
“I will exult and shout,
The land of Shechem I’ll divide
And Succoth portion out.
The land of Gilead is Mine,
Manasseh, too, I own;
My head’s defense is Ephraim,
And Judah is My throne.”

“I made My washbowl Moab’s land, 
On Edom threw My shoe;
So shout aloud, Philistia,
Because of what I do.”
O who is there to bring me to
The city fortified?
And who is there to lead me on 
To Edom as a guide?

But have not You Yourself, O God,
Rejected us once more?
And will You not stand up, O God,
To go with us to war?
Give help against the enemy,
No help does man bestow.
With God we will do valiantly;
He tramples down our foes.

hymns.title: O God, Hear My Cry
hymns.composer: Johann M. Hayden; arr. William Gardiner, Sacred Melodies, II, 1815

verses.text:
O God, hear my cry, give heed to my prayer.
From earth’s farthest end, I call to You there,
When my heart grows faint, it is then that I cry;
Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.

For You’ve always been a refuge for me,
A tower of strength from each enemy.
O let me forever in Your tent abide,
And under Your sheltering wings let me hide.

Before God he’ll sit, enthroned he’ll endure;
Give Your love and truth to make him secure.
So I will forever to Your name sing praise,
That I may my vows pay throughout all my days.

hymns.title: My Cry and Prayer, O God, Attend
hymns.firstLine: My Cry and Prayer, O God, Attend

verses.text:
A refuge You have been for me,
You’ve been against the enemy
A tower strong and true.
Within Your house I will abide,
And underneath Your wings will hide,
Forever safe in You.

For You, O God, my vows have heard,
On me the heritage conferred
Of him Your name that fears.
Long life You to the king will give;
Through generations he will live,
From age to age his years.

Before God’s presence, he’ll abide;
So, love and faithfulness provide,
Preserving him each day.
So, to Your name I’ll always sing,
A song of praise I’ll daily bring,
That I my vows may pay.

hymns.title: My Soul Finds Rest in God Alone
hymns.firstLine: My Soul Finds Rest in God Alone

verses.text:
My soul finds rest in God alone; 
He my salvation is.
My only Rock, Salvation’s fort;
I’m safe, for I am His. 
How long will you press your attack 
To make a person fall 
As though against a sagging fence,
Against a leaning wall?

In God alone my glory is,
And my salvation sure;
My rock of strength is found in God, 
My refuge most secure. 
O people, at all times on Him 
Rely with confidence; 
Pour out your hearts in prayer to Him, 
For God is our defense.

hymns.title: My Soul Finds Rest in God Alone
hymns.firstLine: My Soul Finds Rest in God Alone
hymns.composer: American traditional melody, from William Walker’s Southern Harmony, 1835

verses.text:
My soul finds rest in God alone;
Salvation comes from Him.
He’s my salvation, fortress, rock; 
Unshaken I’ll remain.
How long will you attack a man,
By murder make him fall,
As though he were a tott’ring fence,
Or like a leaning wall?

They plot to bring him toppling down,
In lies they take delight;
And as they bless him with their mouth,
In heart they curse with spite.
Find rest, my soul, in God alone,
For my hope comes from Him.
He’s my salvation, fortress, rock;
Unshaken I’ll remain.

On God alone my glory rests,
And my salvation sure.
God is my mighty rock of strength,
My refuge most secure.
In Him, O people, at all times 
Rely with confidence;
Before Him, now, pour out your heart,
For God is our defense.

All lowborn men are but a breath, 
All high-ranked men a lie;
Together on the balances,
They’re lighter than a sigh.

Don’t in extortion place your hope;
For stolen goods don’t lust.
And though your riches may increase,
On them don’t build your trust.

For God has spoken - twice I heard,
“All power is God’s,” You say.
And mercy, Lord, is Yours as well;
Men’s works You will repay.

hymns.title: O God, You are My God
hymns.firstLine: O God, You are My God
hymns.composer: Andre Campra; arr. G. Duncan Lowe, 1972

verses.text:
O God, You are my God,
And early will I seek for You;
My soul is athirst for You.
My flesh cries out for You
From out a dry and thirsty land,
A land where no water is.
For thus to behold You in splendid strength
I gazed after You in the holy place.
Since Your grace is much more than life,
My lips will give praise to You.

I’ll bless You while I live,
And I will ever lift my hands
To praise and confess Your name.
My soul will be made full
As with all choice and hearty meats;
I’ll praise You with joyful lips.
I think of You thus as I lie in bed
And bring You to mind in the hours of night.
Since You ever have been my help,
Your wings are my shield and joy.

My soul clings fast to You;
Your right hand holds me safely up.
When men would destroy my life,
To depths of earth they go;
They are delivered to the sword,
To jackals become a prey.
The king will rejoice and be glad in God,
And they boast aloud who have sworn in Him,
But the mouth will be made to stop
Of those who declare a lie.

I’ll seek You early, God, my God;
My soul’s athirst for You.
In dry, unwatered, weary lands,
My flesh longs after You.

I’ve longed for You like this before
Within Your holy place,
That there I might behold Your strength,
The glory of Your face.

Because Your love is more than life,
My lips will give You praise.
So I will bless You while I live,
My hands lift in Your name.

My soul, as with the choicest food,
Is fully satisfied;
With shouts of joy upon my lips,
My mouth will praise provide.

hymns.title: And When I Turn My Thoughts to You
hymns.firstLine: And When I Turn My Thoughts to You

verses.text:
And when I turn my thoughts to You
Upon my bed at night,
As watches pass, I meditate
On You with much delight.

For You’re my help; I sing for joy
In shadow of Your wings.
And Your right hand has held me up,
To You my soul now clings.

But they go down to depths of earth
Who’d take my life away;
They are delivered to the sword
To be the jackals’ prey.

The king will then rejoice in God,
And all who by him swear;
For stopped will be the mouths of those
Who do a lie declare.

God, hear my voice, hear my complaint,
Preserve me from my foe.
Hide me from plots of evil men, 
When sinners violent grow,

Whose tongues are sharpened like a sword,
With bitter speech like spears;
To shoot in secret at the just,
They shock and do not fear.

They set their minds on evil plans,
Lay traps, and say, “Who sees?”;
With skill devise injustices,
Man’s heart and thoughts are deep.

But God will shoot a shaft at them 
And wound them all with dread.
So their own tongue will trip them up;
Those seeing shake their head.

Then all will fear and tell God’s work,
Considering His deeds. 
The just find refuge in the LORD,
In Him boast joyfully.

God, hear my voice, hear my complaint,
Preserve me from my foe.
Hide me from plots of evil men, 
When sinners violent grow,

Whose tongues are sharpened like a sword,
With bitter speech like spears;
To shoot in secret at the just,
They shock and do not fear.

They set their minds on evil plans,
Lay traps, and say, “Who sees?”,
With skill devise injustices,
Man’s heart and thoughts are deep.

But God will shoot a shaft at them 
And wound them all with dread.
So their own tongue will trip them up;
Those seeing shake their head.

Then all will fear and tell God’s work,
Considering His deeds. 
The just find refuge in the LORD,
In Him boast joyfully.

Awaiting You in Zion,
Are praise and silence, God; 
And promises completed,
Which men to You have vowed.
Of prayer You are the hearer,
To You will all men come.
Though evil words would crush me,
You for our sins atone.

How blessed is the person
Who is Your chosen one,
The one You have brought near You
And made Your courts his home.
Within Your holy temple
We will be satisfied,
And filled with all the goodness 
Your holy house provides.

O God of our salvation,
You in Your righteousness,
By awesome deeds and wonders
Your answer will express.
You are the One who’s trusted
To earth’s extremity, 
By people who are living
Beyond the farthest sea.

His strength set firm the mountains, 
Pow’r clothes Him evermore,
Who stills the peoples’ clamor,
Makes calm the ocean’s roar.
The far and distant peoples
Behold Your signs with fear;
You make the dawn and sunset
Shout loud with joy and cheer.

You visit earth with showers,
And so enrich the field;
God’s river brims with water,
As You prepare earth’s yield.
You water its rich furrows, 
Its ridges smooth with rain;
You soften earth with showers,
You bless its sprouting grain.

You’ve crowned each year with goodness,
Your paths enrich the ground.
The desert pastures blossom,
With joy the hills resound.
The fields with flocks are covered,
The valleys clothed with grain.
They all rejoice with shouting,
With songs their joy proclaim.

Blessed is the one You’ve chosen,
To live near You, in Your courts.
We are satisfied with good things
In Your house, Your holy place.
God, You answer us, our Savior,
With Your awesome, righteous deeds.

You’re the trust of all earth’s peoples
To the ends of distant seas.
By Your pow’r You placed the mountains;
You have clothed Yourself with strength.
You have calmed the ocean’s roaring,
Turmoil of the nations stilled.

hymns.title: The Far and Distant Peoples Fear
hymns.firstLine: The Far and Distant Peoples Fear

verses.text:
The far and distant peoples fear
The wonders You have made appear.
From dawn to when the sun goes down,
You make their songs of joy resound.
You visit earth, its waters flow;
Great riches on it You bestow.
Great riches on it You bestow.

God’s streams have overflowed with rain,
Earth is prepared for sprouting grain.
You water furrows thoroughly,
And smooth its ridges tenderly.
Your showers have the earth caressed;
In all of this, its growth You blessed.
In all of this, its growth You blessed.

The year with goodness You have crowned,
The pastures prosper and abound.
The hills are clothed with joyfulness,
The meadowlands with flocks are dressed.
The valleys’ fields abound with grain,
They shout and sing, their joy proclaim.
They shout and sing, their joy proclaim.

O all the earth, in joyful shouts, 
To God, your voices raise.
And sing the glory of His name, 
And glorious make His praise.
And glorious make His praise.

To God declare, “How awesome are
The wondrous works you do!”
So great Your strength! Your enemies
In haste submit to You,
In haste submit to You.

Yes, all the earth will worship You,
They praise to You will sing;
And to Your name most glorious
Their songs of praise will bring,
Their songs of praise will bring.

O come, behold the works of God,
His mighty doings see; 
In wondrous works on man’s behalf
How truly great is He! 
How truly great is He!

He turned the sea into dry land,
Their feet a pathway had
Where they then through the river walked
Let us in Him be glad!
Let us in Him be glad!

He rules forever by His might,
On nations keeps His eye.
Let not the proud, rebellious ones
Exalt themselves on high,
Exalt themselves on high!

hymns.title: O All You Peoples, Bless Our God
hymns.firstLine: O All You Peoples, Bless Our God

verses.text:
O all you peoples, bless our God,
Abroad proclaim His praise;
The One who keeps our souls alive,
Our feet from stumbling stays.
For You, O God, have tested us
As silver is refined. 
You caught us in a net, and on
Our backs a load You bind.

You let men trample on our heads;
We passed through fire and flood.
But then at last you brought us to
A place of bounteous good.
And so I’ll come into Your house;
Burnt offerings I’ll pay
To keep the vows my lips had made
When troubles filled my way.

Burnt offerings of fattened beasts
With smoke of rams I’ll take;
And from the cattle and the goats
I will an off’ring make.
All you that fear God, come and hear
What God did for my soul.
For with my mouth I cried to Him,
My tongue did Him extol.

If in my heart I cherished sin,
The Lord then would not hear. 
But surely God has heard my voice,
He to my prayer gave ear.
Forever blessed be our God!
My prayer He has not spurned;
And He has not away from me
His lovingkindness turned.

hymns.title: All Earth to God Raise Joyful Song
hymns.firstLine: All Earth to God Raise Joyful Song

verses.text:
Bless God, O peoples, sound His praise;
He who appoints our soul to live,
And keeps our feet from slipping.
As silver, God, You tested us,
Delivered us into the net,
Oppressed us with a burden.
Men rode o’er us;
We have gone through fire and water
By Your doing.
Yet You brought us forth to freedom.

hymns.title: O God, Give Us Your Blessing
hymns.firstLine: O God, Give Us Your Blessing

verses.text:
O God, give us Your blessing 
Extend to us Your grace,
And cause to shine upon us 
The radiance of Your face;
In order that Your pathways
Would through the earth be known,
That You to every nation 
Would Your salvation show.

hymns.title: O God, Give Us Your Blessing
hymns.firstLine: O God, Give Us Your Blessing

verses.text:
O God, give us Your blessing 
Extend to us Your grace,
And cause to shine upon us 
The radiance of Your face;
In order that Your pathways
Would through the earth be known,
That You to every nation 
Would Your salvation show.

hymns.title: O God, Show Mercy to Us
hymns.firstLine: O God, Show Mercy to Us
hymns.composer: Gustav Holst, 1918; arr. Brian E. Coombs, 2003

verses.text:
O God, show mercy to us, 
And bless us with Your grace;
And cause to shine upon us 
The brightness of Your face; 
So that the whole world over 
May truly know Your way,
And so that Your salvation 
All nations see displayed. 
O God, let peoples praise You; 
Let all the peoples praise.
Let nations come rejoicing 
And songs of gladness raise.

For You will judge the peoples 
With perfect equity;
To nations of the whole earth 
A governor You’ll be.
O God, let peoples praise You; 
Let all the peoples praise.
The earth has brought its bounty 
Throughout its harvest days
Since God, our God, will bless us.
Yes, God will blessing send, 
That all the earth may fear Him 
To its remotest end.

His name is LORD! Be joyful in His presence.
He is a Father to the fatherless,
A judge who helps,
The widow’s cause;
God is within His house of holiness.

God makes a home, a fam’ly for the lonely;
He leads out pris’ners to prosperity.
But in dry lands 
Of wilderness,
There the rebellious ones are left to be.

Let God arise, and scattered far
Be all His enemies.
And let all those who hate Him flee;
Let none before Him stay.
Like smoke drive them away!

O sing to God! O praise His name!
A highway make for Him,
The Rider through the desert wastes!
The LORD - this is His name -
Before Him joy proclaim!

The orphans’ father, widows’ help,
God’s in His holy house.
God leads the pris’ners out to peace,
Gives needy ones a home;
But rebels deserts roam.

hymns.title: When With Your People You Went Forth
hymns.firstLine: When With Your People You Went Forth
hymns.composer: Frederic M.A. Venua; arr. William Gardiner, Sacred Melodies, I, 1812

verses.text:
When with Your people You went forth,
And marched through desert lands, O God,
Earth shook; skies fell before God’s face;
Before God’s presence Sinai quaked,
Before the God of Israel.

O God, You sent abundant rain,
Your weary heritage refreshed.
Your congregation settled there,
And in Your goodness You, O God,
Made rich provision for the poor.

The Lord announces this His word,
Great hosts of women spread the news: 
“The kings of armies flee! They flee!
And she who stays behind at home
Will be there to divide the spoil!”

Though you among the campfires sleep,
You’re like a dove with silver wings,
Whose feathers are a glist’ning gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings,
It looked like snow on Zalmon’s hill.

hymns.title: Bashan’s Mountains
hymns.composer: Traditional Dutch melody; arr. Julius Roentgen, 1906

verses.text:
Bashan’s mountains are majestic,
Bashan’s peaks are strong and fair.
Why do you O rugged mountains 
With deep envy gape and stare
At the hill which God has chosen
To establish as His own? 
There the LORD has made His dwelling,
And it shall remain His home.

Many thousands are God’s chariots
More than thousands, numberless;
With them comes the Lord from Sinai
To His place of holiness.
You’ve ascended to the highest,
Leading captives as Your own;
Gaining gifts from men and rebels,
There the LORD God makes His home.

Praise the Lord our God and Savior;
Daily burdens He relieves.
Our God is a God who saves us,
God the LORD from death sets free.
Surely God will crush in pieces
Heads of every enemy,
And the heads of those persisting,
Working their iniquity.

“I will bring them back from Bashan,”
So the Lord said formerly.
“Surely I will yet retrieve them
From the bottom of the sea
So that you may strike and crush them,
In their blood immerse your feet;
Then your dogs may have their portion,
Feed upon your enemies.”

hymns.title: God, Your Procession Now Comes into View
hymns.firstLine: God, Your Procession Now Comes into View

verses.text:
God, Your procession now comes into view,
My God, my King’s march to the holy place.
Singers, and then musicians after them,
Maidens among them playing tambourines.
Within the congregations, bless our God.

O bless the LORD, the Fount of Israel.
There’s Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them,
And Judah’s princes in their company,
Zebulun’s princes standing by their side,
As well, the princes come from Naphtali.

Your God it is who has commanded strength;
So show to us that You are strong, O God,
As You have done before on our behalf.
Because of Your house in Jerusalem,
Kings will present rich offerings to You.

Chasten the beasts who are among the reeds,
The herd of bulls among the nations’ calves,
Till each is humbled, bringing silver bars;
Scatter the peoples who delight in war.
Egypt sends envoys, Cush appeals to God.

Sing out your praises unto God,
O kingdoms of the earth;
And sing unto the Lord of all
In praise of His great worth, 
In praise of His great worth.

Praise Him who rides from ancient times
In heaven’s highest height.
Behold, He speaks out with His voice,
A voice of pow’r and might,
A voice of pow’r and might.

Declare that God possesses strength;
His majesty is high,
Exalted over Israel,
His strength is in the skies.
His strength is in the skies.

O God, You’re awesome from Your throne
Isr’el’s own God is He,
Who gives His people strength and power;
O let God blessed be!
O let God blessed be!

hymns.title: Save Me, O God
hymns.composer: Andre Campra; arr. G. Duncan Lowe, 1972

verses.text:
Save me, O God, because the mighty waters 
Have come upon my soul on every side. 
I sink in miry depths. There is no foothold;
I am engulfed beneath the water’s tide.
My throat is parched and dry. I’m worn out crying;
My eyes fail while I wait on God for aid.
Those people hating me without a reason
Are more than all the hairs upon my head.

My wrongful, mighty foes seek to destroy me.
I must restore the things I did not steal.
But as for You, O God, You know my folly;
From You my guiltiness I can’t conceal.
My Lord, O LORD of hosts, may those who trust You 
Not ever be ashamed because of me.
May those who seek for You, O God of Isr’el,
Not ever be disgraced because of me.

For Your own sake I have endured derision;
My face is covered with contempt and shame.
I am a foreigner to my own brothers;
And from my mother’s sons I am estranged.
Since for Your house I am consumed with fervor
Those who insult You turn their taunts on me.
And though within my soul I wept with fasting,
Yet even this became reproach to me.

When in my grief I clothed myself in sackcloth,
A laughingstock I then became to them.
Those sitting in the gate now talk about me,
I am the theme of songs by drunken men.
But as for me, I lift my prayer to You, LORD; 
Accept it in the time that pleases You.
In the abundance of Your lovingkindness,
Respond, O God, with Your salvation true.

hymns.title: O Let Their Table Be a Snare
hymns.firstLine: O Let Their Table Be a Snare

verses.text:
O let their table be a snare before them;
When they’re at peace, let it become a trap.
O let their eyes be darkened in their seeing, 
And make their bodies shake without control.

Your indignation be poured out upon them, 
Your burning anger catch them in their flight. 
O let their camp be brought to desolation;
Let not one dwelling in their tents remain.

For they have hounded him that You have smitten, 
Talking about the grief of those You pierced.
Add to their guilt more guiltiness upon them, 
May they not come into Your righteousness.

Out of the book of life let them be blotted,
And let them not be listed with the just.
But as for me, I am in pain, afflicted;
O God, may Your salvation raise me up.

The name of God I with a song
Most cheerfully will praise;
And I in giving thanks to Him
His name will highly raise.

For this will please the Lord far more
Than will the offering
Of any bull with horns or hoofs
Or ox that I may bring.

Let heav’n and earth praise Him, the seas,
And all with which they’re filled.
For God will Zion surely save,
And Judah’s cities build.

They and their children there will live,
Their own possession claim.
The ones inheriting the land,
Are those who love His name.

Hasten, O God, to my rescue;
Hasten to help, O LORD.
Let there be shame and confusion
On those who seek my life.

Turned back be they and dishonored
Who in my hurt delight.
By their disgrace be they covered
Who jeer, “Aha! Aha!”

Let those who seek You be joyful,
Let them be glad in You;
Let those who love Your salvation
Say, “God be magnified!”

hymns.title: In You, O LORD, I Put My Trust
hymns.firstLine: In You, O LORD, I Put My Trust

verses.text:
Save me, my God, from wicked hands,
Hands cruel and unjust;
For LORD, my Lord, You are my hope,
From youth You are my trust.

For I have been sustained by You
Through birth and early days.
You brought me from my mother’s womb;
I’ll give You constant praise.

To many I’m a wondrous sign,
You are my refuge strong.
My mouth is brimming with Your praise
And honor all day long.

hymns.title: Do Not Forsake Me When I’m Old
hymns.firstLine: Do Not Forsake Me When I’m Old

verses.text:
Let all my foes be swallowed up,
And put them all to shame;
Clothe them with scorn who seek my hurt,
Reproach bring on their name.

But as for me, I’ll always hope,
And add to all Your praise.
All day I’ll tell Your saving acts,
Your countless righteous ways.

hymns.title: I’ll Come to Tell the Mighty Deeds
hymns.firstLine: I’ll Come to Tell the Mighty Deeds

verses.text:
I’ll come to tell the mighty deeds
That God the LORD has done;
And I’ll declare Your righteousness,
I’ll speak of Yours alone.
O God, I have been taught by You
From early days of youth;
And all the wonders You have done
I still declare as truth.

And even when I’m old and gray, 
O God, forsake me not,
Until Your strength and pow’r I have
Each generation taught.
For God, Your righteousness extends
Beyond the heights we view;
And You have done such wondrous things,
O God, who is like You?

Though in the past You made me see
Much trouble and distress,
You will revive and raise me up 
From earth’s enclosing depths.
Increase my honor, turn again
To give me peace and rest.
My God, with harps I’ll praise and sing
About Your faithfulness.

O Holy One of Israel,
The harp I will employ;
Redeemed by You, I’ll sing Your praise,
Will shout Your praise with joy. 
My tongue will also speak about
Your justice all day long;
For they are humbled and ashamed
Who seek to do me wrong.

hymns.title: God, Give Your Judgments to the King
hymns.firstLine: God, Give Your Judgments to the King

verses.text:
God, give Your judgments to the king,
And give his son Your righteousness.
He to Your people right will bring,
With justice will Your poor redress.

Mountains will bring prosperity,
The hills bring peace by righteousness.
He’ll judge the poor, their young set free,
And crush the ones who have oppressed.

Long as the sun and moon are known
They’ll fear You through the ages all.
He’ll come as rain on meadows mown,
Like showers on the earth that fall.

The just will flourish in his days,
While lasts the moon will peace extend.
From sea to sea will be his reign,
And from the River to earth’s end.

Nomads will bow to him as king;
Licking the dust, his foes will bend.
Islands and Tarshish gifts will bring,
Sheba and Seba tribute send.

So shall all kings before him fall,
All nations his commands obey.
He’ll save the needy when they call,
Those who are poor and have no aid.

He’ll show the poor his sympathy,
And he will save the needy’s life.
From fraud and force he’ll set them free;
Their blood is precious in his sight.

So he will live, and Sheba’s gold
They’ll as a gift before him lay;
In constant prayer they’ll him uphold,
And they will bless him all the day.

hymns.title: May Waving Grain on Hilltops Thrive
hymns.firstLine: May Waving Grain on Hilltops Thrive

verses.text:
May waving grain on hilltops thrive;
Like Lebanon, its harvest yield.
May people flourish, towns revive,
Like grasses growing in the field,
Like grasses growing in the field.

O may his name forever live;
Yes, like the sun, may his fame last.
By him may people blessings give,
May all the nations call him blessed,
May all the nations call him blessed.

May God be blessed - the LORD alone - 
Blessed be the God of Israel.
For only He has wonders done;
His works all other deeds excel,
His works all other deeds excel.

And may His name of glorious worth
Receive its praise eternally;
And may His glory fill the earth
Amen, Amen; so may it be,
Amen, Amen; so may it be.

hymns.title: O God, Bestow Your Judgments on the King
hymns.firstLine: O God, Bestow Your Judgments on the King

verses.text:
O God, bestow Your judgments on the king,
Your righteousness upon the royal son.
With righteousness Your people he will judge,
Your poor afflicted ones with equity.
So let the mountains bring Your people peace,
And hills bring forth the fruit of righteousness.

The poor among the people he will judge,
And save the children of the indigent.
The strong oppressor he will break apart.
And they will look to You with godly fear
While sun and moon continue to endure;
Through every generation they remain.

He will come down like rain upon the grass,
As showers watering the thirsty ground.
Throughout his reign the righteous ones will thrive,
And peace will flourish while the moon endures.
And he will rule from sea to farthest sea,
And from the River to the ends of earth.

The desert dwellers then will bow to him,
Before him all his foes will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and the coastal lands 
Will come to him and bring an offering;
Sheba’s and Seba’s kings give precious gifts.
All kings will bow, all nations worship him.

hymns.title: He Will Save the Needy
hymns.composer: Traditional South African melody; arr. Brian E. Coombs, 2002

verses.text:
He will save the needy when they call,
Save the poor, and those who have no help.
He has pity on the poor and weak,
And he saves the lives of those in need.
From oppression - and from every violence - 
O he redeems their life and buys them back!
And how precious - precious is their life-blood - 
O how their life is precious in his sight!

May he live, and gold from Sheba’s realm
Then be given as a gift to him.
May the people always pray for him,
May they bless his name throughout the day.
In all regions - and upon the hilltops -
O may there be abundant crops of grain!
Being fruitful - Lebanon with cedars - 
O may the city thrive like grassy fields!

May his name endure forevermore;
May it grow as under shining sun. 
And may people then be blessed in him,
And may all the nations call him blessed.
May the LORD God - who alone does wonders -
O may the God of Israel be blessed!
Blessed be His name - glorious forever - 
O may His glory fill the earth! Amen.

Now blessed be the LORD our God,
The God of Israel;
For He alone does wondrous works,
In glory that excel.

And blessed be His glorious name,
To all eternity.
The whole earth let His glory fill;
Amen, so let it be.

Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
Who alone does wondrous things.
Blessed be His glorious name forever.
Let His glory fill the whole earth. Amen, and Amen.

hymns.title: Yes, God Is Good to Israel
hymns.firstLine: Yes, God Is Good to Israel
hymns.composer: Henri F. Henry, 1864; arr. James G. Walton, 1870

verses.text:
Yes, God is good to Israel,
To every one whose heart is pure.
But as for me, I nearly fell; 
My footsteps were no longer sure.
For I was envious of the proud
And wicked ones with wealth endowed.

For in their death no pains they know;
Their strength is firm from day to day.
They share no part in others’ woe,
Nor plagued as other men are they.
They make their necklace arrogance,
And clothe themselves with violence.

Their people therefore with them turn
To drink from streams that overflow.
“For how,” they say, “can God discern?”
And, “Does the Most High really know?”
Behold, ungodly men are these,
Who gain in wealth and live at ease.

hymns.title: Then Surely I Have Toiled in Vain
hymns.firstLine: Then Surely I Have Toiled in Vain

verses.text:
Then surely I have toiled in vain
To cleanse my heart from all offense,
And vainly from each guilty stain
Have washed my hands in innocence.
Still grievous plagues all day I’ve borne,
And I was chastened every morn.

If I would let my thoughts so lead 
To speak with doubting words this way,
Behold, I then would certainly
The children You have called betray.
But though the facts I tried to see,
The problem deeply troubled me.

I entered then God’s dwelling place
And there I understood their end;
You set them in a slippery place,
And to destruction them You send.
How rapidly destroyed are they,
By sudden terrors swept away!

hymns.title: Yet Constantly I Am with You
hymns.firstLine: Yet Constantly I Am with You

verses.text:
Are You not all I have in heav’n?
None else on earth do I desire.
Though human strength come to an end -
My flesh may fail, my heart expire -
My heart’s strength God Himself will be,
My portion through eternity.

Those far from You will surely die,
Who dealt with You unfaithfully.
But as for me, I will draw nigh.
How good that God is near to me!
I refuge take in God the LORD,
That all Your works I may record.

hymns.title: God, Why Forever Cast Us Off?
hymns.firstLine: God, Why Forever Cast Us Off?

verses.text:
God, why forever cast us off?
Why does Your anger burn
Against the flock of Your own field?
Recall Your gathered ones
You purchased long ago.

Remember them that You redeemed
Your tribe and heritage,
And Zion’s mountain where You live.
O turn Your steps to walk
Where ruin is complete.

Your foes laid waste the holy place;
They shouted in Your halls,
They set their foreign emblems up.
It seemed as if an axe
Had cut down forest trees.

Their axes broke its fine-carved wood;
The holy place they burned.
The place You made Your name to dwell,
Now even to the ground 
They have profaned and razed.

“O let us crush them utterly!”
So did their hearts declare.
They burned each God-appointed place.
No prophet now, no signs,
And none who knows how long!

How long, O God, will foes insult
And always scorn Your name?
O why do You hold back Your hand?
Reach forth with Your right hand
To end and to destroy!

hymns.title: Yet God My King Brings Forth
hymns.firstLine: Yet God My King Brings Forth

verses.text:
Yet God my King brings forth of old
Salvation in the earth.
The sea You parted by Your strength;
You smote Leviathan,
And fed him to the beasts.

You opened springs; You dried the streams.
Both day and night are Yours;
You have ordained both light and sun.
You gave the earth its bounds,
And made the heat and cold.

O bring to mind the covenant;
See how the land grows dark,
Filled with the dens of violence.
Let not the meek be shamed,
But let them praise Your name.

Arise, O God! Take up Your cause!
Recall the scorn of fools!
Recall Your adversaries’ cries,
The raging noise of foes
Which rises endlessly!

hymns.title: To You, O God, We Render Thanks
hymns.firstLine: To You, O God, We Render Thanks

verses.text:
To You, O God, we render thanks, 
To You give thanks sincere,
Because Your wondrous works declare 
That Your great name is near.
“When My appointed time is come, 
I’ll judge with even hand. 
Though earth and all its dwellers melt, 
I make its pillars stand.”

“’Boast not!’” I said to boastful men,
To vile men, ‘Lift no horn!
Do not lift up your horn on high, 
Nor speak with haughty scorn!’”
From east or west or wilderness
None comes to glorify.
But God is Judge, debasing one,
Another raising high.

The LORD’s hand holds a foaming cup
Which potent wine contains;
He pours and makes the wicked drink
Until the dregs he drains.
But I forever will declare, 
To Jacob’s God sing praise;
All horns of sinners He’ll cut off,
The righteous’ horns are raised.

hymns.title: To You, O God, We Render Thanks
hymns.firstLine: To You, O God, We Render Thanks

verses.text:
To You, O God, we render thanks, 
To You give thanks sincere,
Because Your wondrous works declare 
That Your great name is near.
“When My appointed time is come, 
I’ll judge with even hand. 
Though earth and all its dwellers melt, 
I make its pillars stand.”

“’Boast not!’” I said to boastful men,
To vile men, ‘Lift no horn!
Do not lift up your horn on high, 
Nor speak with haughty scorn!’”
From east or west or wilderness
None comes to glorify.
But God is Judge, debasing one,
Another raising high.

The LORD’s hand holds a foaming cup
Which potent wine contains;
He pours and makes the wicked drink
Until the dregs he drains.
But I forever will declare, 
To Jacob’s God sing praise;
All horns of sinners He’ll cut off,
The righteous’ horns are raised.

hymns.title: God Is Truly Known in Judah
hymns.firstLine: God Is Truly Known in Judah

verses.text:
You’re more glorious and majestic
Than the mountains filled with prey.
Brave and valiant ones You plundered,
Now they slumber in the grave;
Though they once were mighty warriors,
None can lift his hands to save.

Horse and rider both lie sleeping,
Cast down into death’s dark night.
You rebuked them, God of Jacob - 
Awe-inspiring in Your might!
Once Your anger has been kindled,
Who can stand before Your sight?

You from heaven spoke Your verdict,
And the earth in fear was still.
Saving all the earth’s afflicted,
God arose to do His will.
With what’s left from wrath You’re girded;
Human wrath will praise You still.

Give the LORD your God your promise,
And fulfill your vows sincere.
Let all those around bring tribute
To the One to be revered.
He brings low the pride of princes,
And by kings of earth is feared.

hymns.title: God Is Truly Known in Judah
hymns.firstLine: God Is Truly Known in Judah

verses.text:
You’re more glorious and majestic
Than the mountains filled with prey.
Brave and valiant ones You plundered,
Now they slumber in the grave;
Though they once were mighty warriors,
None can lift his hands to save.

Horse and rider both lie sleeping,
Cast down into death’s dark night.
You rebuked them, God of Jacob - 
Awe-inspiring in Your might!
Once Your anger has been kindled,
Who can stand before Your sight?

You from heaven spoke Your verdict,
And the earth in fear was still.
Saving all the earth’s afflicted,
God arose to do His will.
With what’s left from wrath You’re girded;
Human wrath will praise You still.

Give the LORD your God your promise,
And fulfill your vows sincere.
Let all those around bring tribute
To the One to be revered.
He brings low the pride of princes,
And by kings of earth is feared.

hymns.title: My Voice to God, Aloud I Plead
hymns.firstLine: My Voice to God, Aloud I Plead

verses.text:
My voice to God, aloud I plead!
My voice to God, He will me heed!
I sought the Lord, I was distressed,
I gave my outstretched hands no rest.
My restless soul all through the night
No comfort found in coming light.
With thoughts of God my fears arise;
My failing spirit faints with sighs.

You do not let my eyelids close;
I am made speechless by my woes.
The days of old I think upon,
The years that long ago have gone.
I ponder songs I sang at night;
My heart and spirit search for light.
Forever will the Lord reject?
Can I His favor not expect?

Forever has His kindness ceased?
And is He from His word released?
Did God forget to show His grace?
Does wrath His mercy now replace?
Then I replied, “Such questions show
That I my weakness need to know.
The Most High has a firm right hand
That through the years will changeless stand.”

The LORD’s deeds I remember all,
Your wondrous works of old recall.
I’ll ponder all that You have done
And weigh Your mighty acts, each one.

O God, Your ways most holy are.
What god can with our God compare?
You are the God by wonders known;
Among the peoples, strength You’ve shown.

You by Your arm Your people freed,
The sons of Jacob, Joseph’s seed.
O God, the waters sighted You,
Deep seas shook when You came in view.

From clouds the rain in torrents poured,
Across the sky tornadoes roared.
The world was lit when lightning flashed,
Earth trembled when the thunder crashed.

Great waters formed a path for You,
Your footprints hidden from our view.
Your people like a flock were fed,
By Moses and by Aaron led.

O come, my people, to my law
Attentively give ear;
The words that from my mouth proceed
Incline yourselves to hear.
My mouth will speak a parable,
The sayings dark of old,
Which we have listened to and known
As by our fathers told.

We’ll from their children hide them not,
But tell the age to come
The praises of the LORD, His strength,
The wonders He has done.
His word He unto Jacob gave,
His law to Israel,
Which He our fathers did command
To teach their children well.

That children yet unborn might know,
And their descendants lead,
To trust in God, recall God’s works,
And His commandments heed;
And not be what their fathers were - 
Rebellious through and through,
For they would not correct their hearts,
Nor unto God stay true.

O come, my people, to my law
Attentively give ear;
The words that from my mouth proceed
Incline yourselves to hear.
My mouth will speak a parable,
The sayings dark of old,
Which we have listened to and known
As by our fathers told.

We’ll from their children hide them not,
But tell the age to come
The praises of the LORD, His strength,
The wonders He has done.
His word He unto Jacob gave,
His law to Israel,
Which He our fathers did command
To teach their children well.

That children yet unborn might know,
And their descendants lead,
To trust in God, recall God’s works,
And His commandments heed;
And not be what their fathers were - 
Rebellious through and through,
For they would not correct their hearts,
Nor unto God stay true.

hymns.title: Ephraim’s Sons
hymns.composer: Johann G. Nageli; arr. Lowell Mason, 1836

verses.text:
Ephraim’s sons, though armed with bows,
In battle did retreat.
They in God’s law refused to walk,
His cov’nant would not keep.

All of His deeds they soon forgot,
His miracles of might,
In Egypt’s land, in Zoan’s field,
Before their fathers’ sight.

He split the sea to let them pass,
The waters stood aside;
By day He led them with a cloud,
And fire at night to guide.

hymns.title: Yet in the Desert Still They Sinned
hymns.firstLine: Yet in the Desert Still They Sinned

verses.text:
Yet in the desert still they sinned,
And from the Most High turned.
They tested God, demanding food
And all for which they yearned.
They spoke against their God and said,
“Can even God provide
A table in the wilderness
That we may be supplied?”

“Behold, He struck the rock, and out
Gushed streams of water sweet;
But can He give His people bread
And furnish them with meat?”
Because the LORD heard this, His wrath
Was kindled into flame;
On Jacob, and on Israel
His indignation came.

For they did not believe in God
Nor trust His saving love.
But still He opened heaven’s doors,
Commanded skies above,
And rained His manna down on them;
From heaven gave them bread.
And man partook of angels’ food,
Abundantly was fed.

hymns.title: In Heav’n He Made the East Wind Blow
hymns.firstLine: In Heav’n He Made the East Wind Blow

verses.text:
In heav’n He made the east wind blow,
The south wind did command;
He rained down meat on them like dust,
And birds like ocean sand.

He let them fall inside their camp
By tents on every side.
And so they ate till they were filled;
Their greed He satisfied.

But while their mouths were crammed with food
God’s wrath upon them fell;
He killed their strong young men, cut down
The best of Israel.

And yet despite His miracles,
They sinned in unbelief;
So He cut off their futile lives,
Their years with sudden grief.

hymns.title: They’d Turn and Seek God Eagerly
hymns.firstLine: They’d Turn and Seek God Eagerly
hymns.composer: Thomas Est, The Whole Book of Psalmes, 1592; arr. George Kirbye

verses.text:
They’d turn and seek God eagerly
When He had made some die;
Then they remembered God, their Rock,
Their Savior, God Most High.

But Him they served with empty words,
And with their tongue they lied;
Their heart was not sincere toward Him,
His cov’nant they denied.

Yet He, instead of killing them,
Forgave iniquity,
And in compassion He restrained
His wrath repeatedly.

His anger He does not stir up.
That they are flesh He knows
A wind that never does return
When once it comes and goes.

These rebels in the wilderness
Kept grieving Him again,
Kept testing Isr’el’s Holy One,
And so to God brought pain!
His pow’r in freeing them from foes
They would not keep in mind - 
The miracles in Zoan’s field,
In Egypt, mighty signs.

He turned their rivers into blood,
Which could not quench their thirst.
He sent devouring swarms of flies,
With frogs their land He cursed.
Their crops by insects were destroyed,
To locusts, all was lost.
He killed their tender vines with hail,
Their sycamores with frost.

He struck their flocks with lightning bolts,
With hail their herds destroyed.
In anger, wrath, and hostile rage,
Death’s angels He deployed.
He for His anger smoothed a path,
They were not spared from death;
But striking with a deadly plague,
He took away their breath.

Then He struck down in Egypt’s land
Their firstborn sons, their pride,
Until in all the tents of Ham
Their heirs of strength had died.
But His own people forth like sheep
He brought with guiding hand,
And led His people like a flock
Across the desert land.

He led them safely, unafraid;
The sea engulfed their foes.
He brought them to His holy land,
The hills His right hand chose.
Before them He drove nations out,
From lands and from their tents;
Allotted these to Isr’el’s tribes
For their inheritance.

Yet they rebelled, they tested God;
The Most High’s law they spurned.
As faithless as their fathers were,
Like treach’rous bow, they turned.

Their shrines and idols angered Him,
Provoked His jealousy.
God heard and turned from Israel,
He spurned them angrily.

His place in Shiloh He has left,
The tent He made with men.
To exile He gave up His strength,
To foes His glory then.

He gave His people to the sword,
Allowed them to be killed.
Against His own inheritance
With anger He was filled.

Their young men were devoured by fire,
Their maidens left unwed;
And when their priests fell by the sword,
No tears their widows shed.

hymns.title: As When Wine Makes the Soldier Bold
hymns.firstLine: As When Wine Makes the Soldier Bold

verses.text:
As when wine makes the soldier bold,
As one wakes with a start;
The Lord drove back His enemies,
Whose shame shall not depart.

Then He rejected Joseph’s tent,
The tribe of Ephraim.
But He the tribe of Judah chose,
Mount Zion, loved by Him.

Like heights He built His holy place,
Forever firm to keep.
He for His servant David chose,
Took him from guarding sheep.

From tending ewes He brought him out
To shepherd Jacob well,
To care for His inheritance,
His chosen Israel.

So with integrity of heart
Them faithfully he fed;
And with his understanding hands,
He guided as he led.

O God, to Your inheritance
The nations entered in,
Your house defiled, in ruins laid
Jerusalem.

Flesh of Your servants they have cast
To heaven’s birds for meat;
They gave the bodies of Your saints
For beasts to eat.

Their blood about Jerusalem
Like water has been shed;
There was no one to bury them
When they were dead.

To all our neighbors we’ve become
Objects of their reproach,
A laughingstock to all who now
On us encroach.

How long, O LORD? Your wrath toward us
Will You forever turn?
And will Your jealousy, like fire, 
Forever burn?

On heathen nations pour Your wrath,
Who call not on Your name;
For Jacob they devour, and waste 
His fields in flame.

hymns.title: O Charge Us Not with Former Sins
hymns.firstLine: O Charge Us Not with Former Sins

verses.text:
O charge us not with former sins,
But Your compassion show.
Come quickly, meet us in our need;
We are brought low.

O God of our salvation, help!
To Your name glory take!
Deliver us; forgive our sins
For Your name’s sake.

Do nations say, “Where is their God?”
Let nations know instead
Your vengeance for your servants’ blood
Which has been shed.

O let the pris’ner’s sighing groans
Ascend to You on high;
Preserve them by Your mighty arm,
Those doomed to die.

And back upon our neighbors turn,
In sevenfold reward,
Reproachful words which they have cast
On You, O Lord.

So we Your people, Your own flock
Forever thank Your name;
We will to generations all
Your praise proclaim.

Hear, O hear us, Isr’el’s Shepherd,
Who drives forth Joseph like a flock.
From the cherubim, O shine forth;
Rise in valor that we be saved.
So arise in sight of Ephraim,
And Manasseh and Benjamin.
God, we pray, O turn us, bring us back;
Shine Your face on us, we’ll be saved!

O how long, Lord God of Armies
Burns Your wrath at Your people’s prayer?
With the bread of tears You feed them,
And full measure of tears they drink.
Strife You make us to our neighbors,
And our foes laugh at us in scorn.
God of Armies, turn us, bring us back;
Shine Your face on us, we’ll be saved!

You brought forth a vine from Egypt,
And to plant it drove nations out.
You made room to root it deeply,
And it flourished and filled the land.
Then its shadow wrapped the mountains,
And its boughs hid the cedars tall.
To the sea it thrust great branches forth,
And young shoots to the mighty stream.

Why have You torn down its fences?
It is plucked by each passing hand.
Forest boars have gnawed upon it,
And wild creatures have pastured there.
Turn again, O God of Armies,
Look from heav’n, visit this Your vine.
So uphold what Your right hand did plant,
And the son You raised up in strength.

hymns.title: To God Our Strength
hymns.composer: J.L. Macbeth Bain, c. 1840-1925; arr. Brian E. Coombs, 2004

verses.text:
To God our Strength, to Jacob’s God, 
A song and shout now raise!
With psalm and timbrel, harp and lute, 
Awake to joyous praise!
At each new moon the trumpet blow 
For solemn festal days.

This is the law of Jacob’s God, 
For Isr’el His command.
This witness He in Joseph set, 
When he ruled Egypt’s land.
I heard a tongue I did not know
And could not understand.

“I from his shoulders took the load, 
His burdened hands found rest.
You called in trouble; My response
In thunder I expressed.
And by the streams of Meribah, 
I put you to the test.”

“Hear, O My people, I will speak: 
O Isr’el, listen now!
Let no strange god be in your midst;
And to them do not bow.
I am the LORD your God who saved -
From Egypt brought you out.”

“O that My people would Me hear, 
And Isr’el choose My way!
How quickly I would subjugate 
Their every enemy!
Upon their adversaries all 
My outstretched hand I’d lay.”

“Then all who hate the LORD would cringe, 
In fear and dread abide.
But Isr’el with the finest wheat 
I’d always keep supplied.
Yes, I with honey from the rock 
Would keep you satisfied.”

God is in His congregation;
Judge among the gods He stands.
How long will you judge unjustly,
Favoring the wicked hands?

Gods you are, I have declared it,
You are sons of Him Most High;
Yet you’ll fall like other princes,
And as common men you’ll die.

Now, O God, arise, we pray You,
And the earth to judgment call;
For You, as Your own possession,
Shall inherit nations all.

God is in His congregation;
Judge among the gods He stands.
How long will you judge unjustly,
Favoring the wicked hands?

Gods you are, I have declared it,
You are sons of Him Most High;
Yet you’ll fall like other princes,
And as common men you’ll die.

Now, O God, arise, we pray You,
And the earth to judgment call;
For You, as Your own possession,
Shall inherit nations all.

hymns.title: Do Not Be Silent, God
hymns.composer: Andre Campra; arr. G. Duncan Lowe, 1972

verses.text:
Do not be silent, God, or unresponding!
Do not remain at rest, O Mighty One!
For now Your foes arouse and make a clamor;
Your bitter enemies lift up the head.
Against Your people now they plot in secret;
They meet to work against Your hidden ones.
They say, “Let us go up and end their nation.
The name of Israel shall be no more!”

Treat them like Midian, like Jabin’s army.
Treat them like Sisera at Kishon’s brook.
At Endor they were all annihilated, 
And they became like dung upon the ground.
Like Zebah, Zalmunna, Oreb, and Ze-eb, 
Those chiefs who tried to seize the land of God.
My God, O make them be like whirling dust clouds;
Make them like bits of chaff before the wind.

Like fire that burns the woods, like flames of lightning,
Pursue them with Your storms and strike with fear.
Fill up their faces with humiliation,
And let them come, O LORD, to seek Your name.
Let them be terrified and shamed forever,
And let them be dismayed and be destroyed.
Let them know You alone - whose name is Yahweh - 
You are the One Most High o’er all the earth.

How lovely, Lord of hosts, to me
The tabernacles of Your grace!
O how I long, yes, faint to see
The LORD’s own courts, His dwelling place!
My heart and flesh with joy draw nigh;
As to the living God I cry.

The sparrow has her place of rest;
The swallow through Your kindly care
Has found where she may build her nest
And brood her young in safety there.
Your altars as my rest I sing,
O Lord of hosts, my God, my King.

Blessed they who in Your house abide;
To You they ever render praise.
Blessed they who in Your strength confide,
And in whose heart are pilgrims’ ways.
They make the vale of tears a spring,
With showers of blessings covering.

Advancing still from strength to strength
They go where other pilgrims trod,
Till each to Zion comes at length
And stands before the face of God.
Lord God of hosts, my pleading hear;
O Jacob’s God, to me give ear.

For God the Lord is shield and sun;
The Lord will grace and glory give.
No good will He withhold from one
Who does uprightly walk and live.
O LORD of hosts, that one is blessed,
Who makes his trust upon You rest.

hymns.title: Your Dwelling Places, LORD
hymns.composer: Traditional English carol; arr. Ralph Vaughan-Williams, 1919

verses.text:
Your dwelling places, LORD of hosts,
How beautiful they are to me.
The LORD’s courts are my soul’s desire, 
I’m yearning for them eagerly.
I to the living God cry out, 
With joy my heart and body shout!

My God, My King, within Your house
The sparrow has a dwelling there.
O LORD of hosts, Your altars are
Where swallows choose their young to bear.
Blessed all who in Your house do live,
To You their praise they ever give.

Those finding strength in You are blessed,
With pilgrims’ hearts they onward reach,
The valley’s tears they turn to springs,
While rain with blessings covers each.
They, gaining strength, toward Zion run,
Before God then appears each one.

O hear my prayer, LORD God of hosts;
O Jacob’s God, give ear to me. 
With favor, God, look on our shield,
The face of Your anointed see.

Much better one day in Your courts 
Compared to thousands spent outside!
I’d rather as God’s doorman stand
Than in the wicked’s tents reside.

O LORD, unto Your land You showed
Your favor graciously bestowed;
The captive Jacob You set free,
Restored his wealth and liberty.

Forgiven have Your people been,
And You have covered all their sin.
From us You’ve taken all Your wrath,
And turned from Your fierce anger’s path.

So now, O God our Savior, turn!
Let indignation cease to burn!
Will You forever angry stay?
From age to age Your wrath display?

Will You not give us life once more,
Your people’s joy in You restore?
O LORD, Your lovingkindness show,
And Your salvation now bestow.

hymns.title: I’ll Hear What God the LORD Will Say
hymns.firstLine: I’ll Hear What God the LORD Will Say

verses.text:
I’ll hear what God the LORD will say:
Peace to His people He’ll convey;
To godly ones He’s promised this,
If they refrain from foolishness.

His saving help is surely near 
To those who worship Him in fear,
That glory great may ever dwell
Within the land of Israel.

Together met are truth and grace,
While righteousness and peace embrace;
True faithfulness springs from the ground,
From heaven righteousness looks down.

The LORD will give us what is good;
Our land will yield abundant food.
Before Him righteousness shall go,
Which for his feet a path will show.

LORD, listen and answer; O hear me, I pray.
I, needy and poor, cry to You.
Watch over my soul; save Your servant, O God;
Devoted, I’m trusting in You.

Since all the day long I am crying to You,
Toward me, Lord, Your mercy renew.
Bring joy to the soul of Your servant, O Lord;
I lift up my soul unto You.

You truly, O Lord, are forgiving and good,
Abounding in kindness and love
To all those who call to You. LORD, hear my prayer;
My pleading attend from above.

In day of my trouble upon You I’ll call;
An answer for me You’ll prepare.
Among all the gods, LORD, there’s no one like You,
And no works with Yours can compare.

All nations created by You, Lord, will come,
And bowing, Your name they will laud.
Because You are great and great wonders have done;
For You, and You only, are God.

Your way teach me, LORD; I will walk in Your truth;
Unite my heart Your name to fear.
My Lord and my God, with my whole heart I’ll praise,
And ever Your name will revere.

For great are Your love and Your kindness to me;
My soul You have freed from the grave.
O God, violent men and the proud seek my life,
Forgetful of You and Your praise.

Lord, merciful God, full of grace, slow to wrath,
Abounding in truth and in love,
Return unto me; Your rich grace now bestow;
Your servant make strong from above.

The son of Your handmaid deliver and save;
A sign of Your goodness renew,
That all those who hate me may see and be shamed.
My help, LORD, and strength are in You.

The LORD’s foundation has been set
Upon the holy hills;
He loves the gates of Zion more
Than homes where Jacob dwells.

About you glorious things are said,
O city of our God:
“I will make mention of the lands
Where I am known abroad.”

“Philistia, Egypt, Babylon,
And Tyre together share
Along with Ethiopia:
’That this is one born there!’”

Of Zion it will be declared:
“Each one was born in her.”
Behold, the Most High will Himself
Establish her secure.

The LORD, in listing citizens,
Notes, “He was born there, too.”
The choristers and minstrels sing,
“My springs are found in you.”

O city of our God:
